text:
Ava: Heads-up — product asked for a unified GPU utilization dashboard for Hosted + Dedicated. Need input on metrics we can realistically expose from runtime/infra. Key asks: SM occupancy, per-GPU memory used/total, queue depth (pending requests), and pool_capacity vs allocated_capacity. Can infra/runtime confirm signal names and cardinality?

Marco: I can emit occupancy and memory from runtime, but we need to agree on semantics. "SM occupancy" for us is fraction of active warps vs max warps, sampled per-SM every 1s. That yields high cardinality if we tag per-sm. Suggest aggregating to GPU level: `gpu_sm_occupancy{gpu_id,model,pool}` as a 0-1 gauge averaged across SMs.

Priya: From infra side, we can stamp pool_id, region, and deployment_type (hosted|dedicated). We prefer not to include model name with full cardinality in raw metrics — maybe include model_family or model_size tag. High-cardinality label combinations blow up TSDB.

Ava: Good point on labels. Product wants drill-down by model variant sometimes though. Can we keep a low-cardinality metric for dashboards and an optional high-cardinality sampling stream (event log) for debugging?

Marco: Yes — runtime can emit two streams: `gpu_sm_occupancy_agg{pool_id,region,deployment_type,model_family}` (1s sample) and a separate trace events export to object storage for per-model traces on demand.

Diego: Console/UX here — dashboards need 1m aggregations for charts, 10s for alerting windows. Also need a derived metric: capacity_usage = allocated_capacity / pool_capacity. Will that be computed upstream or in the console?

Priya: infra prefers computing capacity_usage upstream so it can be used in routing policies and alert rules. We'll emit `pool_capacity_total` and `pool_allocated_units` gauges with the same labels.

Sam: Eng-SRE: alerting thresholds proposals: for Hosted pools, alert when `gpu_sm_occupancy_agg` 5m avg > 0.85 and queue_length 1m p99 > 4 for 3 consecutive minutes. For Dedicated, thresholds are higher but alert to customer-facing ops. Thoughts?

Jenna: Product: we need the latency impact column too. If occupancy goes up, we should correlate token latency tail. Can we emit `token_latency_p90/p99` per pool?

Marco: Token latency is inferred at runtime; we can export `token_latency_p50/p90/p99` per deployment. Keep p99 at 1m window. Labeling same as other metrics.

Ava: Back to cardinality — model_family + deployment + pool_id + region is okay. model_variant/model_timestamp not okay in metrics. We'll keep per-variant traces as object logs.

Priya: Storage/retention: infra needs to cap retention for high-card metrics. Suggest: metrics (low-card) retained 30d, high-card traces 7d in hot storage then cold. Need approval from finance for ingestion increased costs.

Diego: Dashboard UX: please standardize metric names and label keys. Console will map: `pool_id -> Pool` and `deployment_type -> Mode`. Also want common units on charts and built-in alert templates.

Ava: Proposed metric list (please review):

gpu_sm_occupancy_agg{pool_id,region,deployment_type,model_family} gauge
gpu_memory_used_bytes{pool_id,region} gauge
gpu_memory_total_bytes{pool_id,region} gauge
pool_capacity_total{pool_id,region,deployment_type,capacity_class} gauge
pool_allocated_units{pool_id,region,deployment_type,capacity_class} gauge
queue_length{pool_id,region,deployment_type} gauge
token_latency_p50/p90/p99{pool_id,region,deployment_type,model_family} summary

Marco: Looks fine. Change request: `gpu_memory_*` should avoid `gpu_id` in dashboard metrics to reduce cardinality. Keep `gpu_id` only in a debug metric stream.

Priya: We'll add `capacity_class` label (e.g., burst, reserved) so console can filter SLAs.

Sam: Also recommend `queue_wait_time_mean` as a metric (helps separate long queues from short spikes).

Ava: Routing policy implications: API team may want to route traffic away from pools with high occupancy automatically. That requires a stable, low-latency metric feed to the router. How fast can runtime provide the occupancy metric?

Marco: We can push a 5s occupancy feed to the routing service for fast decisions, separate from Prom/long-term metrics. That feed will be expressed over gRPC with the following contract: `PoolMetric { pool_id, occupancy, queue_length, timestamp }`. Need eng-infra signoff for auth and fanout.

Priya: We can host a small fanout service. Auth via mTLS and JWTs. Also need to ensure we don't exceed 10k TPS to routing. Provide sampling/aggregation knobs.

Diego: Console: We'll surface both long-term charts and a "live preview" using the 5s feed. UX wants clear labeling which source is used.

Ava: Action items agreed:
- Marco: implement `gpu_sm_occupancy_agg` and `token_latency` exports, plus 5s routing feed prototype (ETA: Thu).
- Priya: add `pool_capacity_total`, `pool_allocated_units`, `capacity_class` labels, and fanout service + auth (ETA: Fri).
- Diego: draft dashboard wireframe + alert templates (ETA: Mon)
- Sam: define final alert thresholds and runbook entries (ETA: Mon)
- Jenna/Product: confirm model_family taxonomy to use as label (ETA: Tue)

Marco: noted. I'll post example protobuf for routing feed in this thread when ready.

ops-bot: deploybot: runtime/occupancy-feed v0.1 deployed to staging at 1768123810 :rocket:

Ava: Thanks all — will sync again after prototypes. :thumbsup:
